instructions.name: ame.acquire
instructions.description: Requests AME resource ownership; see <<ame-backend-management-operators>>.

instructions.name: ame.release
instructions.description: Releases AME resource ownership; see <<ame-backend-management-operators>>.
instructions.operation: release the AME resources associated with the current context

instructions.name: agettyp
instructions.description:
Gets the 32-bit datatype descriptor of an `Acc` register by reading from `Ad`
and zero-extending it to XLEN in `X[xd]`.

instructions.name: asettyp
instructions.description:
Sets the datatype of an `Acc` register and clears every physical storage bit of
the accumulator to zero.  This is a raw-bit clear, not conversion to the new
datatype's semantic zero.  The new 32-bit descriptor is `X[xs1][31:0]`; any
upper X-register bits are ignored.

instructions.name: mabs.ew
instructions.description: Elementwise absolute value of the tensor in `ms1`, stored into `md`.

instructions.name: mabsdiff.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise absolute difference of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.
Used for L1 distance and error metrics.

instructions.name: mabsdiff.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise absolute difference between a scalar constant from integer
register `xs1` and every element of square `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
The type of the scalar is determined by `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`. The scalar is converted
to the datatype of `ms2` before the operation and then applied to every element position `i`:
+
md[i] = |xs1 - ms2[i]|
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: madd.ew
instructions.description: Vector addition of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.

instructions.name: madd.ew.x
instructions.description:
Adds a scalar constant from integer register `xs1` to every element of square `ms2`,
stored into `md`.
+
The type of the scalar is determined by `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`. The scalar is converted
to the datatype of `ms2` before the operation and then applied to every element position `i`:
+
md[i] = xs1 + ms2[i]
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mand.ew
instructions.description: Elementwise bitwise AND of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.

instructions.name: mand.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise bitwise AND of a scalar constant from integer register `xs1`
with every element of square `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
The type of the scalar is determined by `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`. The scalar is converted
to the datatype of `ms2` before the operation and then applied to every element position `i`:
+
md[i] = xs1 & ms2[i]
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mandnot.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise bitwise AND of `ms1` with the bitwise complement of `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
Useful for masking and bit-field manipulation: bits set in `ms2` are cleared in the result.

instructions.name: mandnot.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise bitwise AND of a scalar constant from integer register `xs1`
with the bitwise complement of every element of square `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
The type of the scalar is determined by `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`. The scalar is converted
to the datatype of `ms2` before the operation and then applied to every element position `i`:
+
md[i] = xs1 & ~ms2[i]
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mcmovge.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise two-way conditional move using the non-negative sign of `ms1` as predicate.
+
For each element, `md[i] = ms2[i]` if `ms1[i] >= 0` (sign bit clear),
otherwise `md[i]` is left unchanged.
+
`md` is both a source and destination: when the predicate is false (sign bit set),
the existing element in `md` is preserved.  `ms1` serves as the predicate register:
any non-negative value is treated as true.
+
Complementary to `mcmovlt.ew`.

instructions.name: mcmovlt.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise two-way conditional move using the sign of `ms1` as predicate.
+
For each element, `md[i] = ms2[i]` if `ms1[i] < 0` (sign bit set),
otherwise `md[i]` is left unchanged.
+
`md` is both a source and destination: when the predicate is false (sign bit clear),
the existing element in `md` is preserved.  `ms1` serves as the predicate register:
any negative value is treated as true.
+
Complementary to `mcmovge.ew`.

instructions.name: mcmpge.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise greater-or-equal comparison of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
For each element, `md[i]` is set to the canonical true value (-1, all bits set) if
`ms1[i] >= ms2[i]`, otherwise `md[i]` is set to the canonical false value (0).
+
Floating-point comparisons follow IEEE 754 semantics.
Complementary to `mcmplt.ew`; both forms are provided to ensure correct behavior
in the presence of NaN, +∞, and −∞.

instructions.name: mcmpge.ew.x
instructions.description:
Compares a scalar constant from integer register `xs1` against every element of square
`ms2`, storing -1 (all bits set) where the scalar is greater than or equal to the element,
and 0 otherwise, into `md`.
+
The type of the scalar is determined by `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`. The scalar is converted
to the datatype of `ms2` before the operation and then applied to every element position `i`:
+
md[i] = (xs1 >= ms2[i]) ? -1 : 0
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mcmplt.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise less-than comparison of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
For each element, `md[i]` is set to the canonical true value (-1, all bits set) if
`ms1[i] < ms2[i]`, otherwise `md[i]` is set to the canonical false value (0).
+
Floating-point comparisons follow IEEE 754 semantics.
Complementary to `mcmpge.ew`; both forms are provided to ensure correct behavior
in the presence of NaN, +∞, and −∞.

instructions.name: mcmplt.ew.x
instructions.description:
Compares a scalar constant from integer register `xs1` against every element of square
`ms2`, storing -1 (all bits set) where the scalar is strictly less than the element,
and 0 otherwise, into `md`.
+
The type of the scalar is determined by `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`. The scalar is converted
to the datatype of `ms2` before the operation and then applied to every element position `i`:
+
md[i] = (xs1 < ms2[i]) ? -1 : 0
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mcolbcast.ew.x
instructions.synopsis: Broadcast one column to all columns
instructions.description:
Broadcasts column `c` (from integer register `xs1`) of `ms1` to every column of `md`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = ms1[i, c]
+
If `c` is outside `[0, sqrt(AME_NELEM))`, an `Illegal Instruction` exception is raised.
+
The `xs1` operand is a control scalar: its low 32 bits are interpreted as an
unsigned integer column index.  It does not read `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]` and does not undergo
AME datatype conversion.
+
The common datatype size is no smaller than `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`; packed
datatypes are not supported.

instructions.name: mcolgather.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise column gather: for each element in each row, uses the corresponding index from `ms2`
to select a column from the same row of `ms1`, and stores the result into `md`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = ms1[i, ms2[i,j]]
+
`ms2` provides integer column indices in the range `[0, sqrt(AME_NELEM))`.
An out-of-range index raises an `Illegal Instruction` exception.
+
The common datatype size is no smaller than `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`; packed
datatypes are not supported.

instructions.name: mcolid.ew
instructions.synopsis: Write zero-based column index to every element
instructions.description:
Writes to each element of the M register group `md` the zero-based index of
the column containing that element.  With `N = sqrt(AME_NELEM)`, every
element of column `j` receives the value `j`, for `0 <= j < N`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = j
+
The index value is represented in the destination datatype `Md[md]`.  The
destination datatype must be a supported *integer* datatype in which the
largest index `N-1` is exactly representable; otherwise `amestatus.UN` is
set and no register is written.
+
Together with `<<ame:doc:inst:mrowid_ew,mrowid.ew>>`, this instruction forms
the index group of the 1-dimensional elementwise instructions, typically
used to materialize coordinate operands for gather, scatter, and predication
sequences.

instructions.name: mcolshift.ew.x
instructions.synopsis: Elementwise column shift by scalar offset
instructions.description:
Elementwise column shift of `ms1` by offset `c`, obtained by interpreting the
low 32 bits of integer register `xs1` as a signed two's-complement integer,
stored into `md`.  This fixed-type control operand does not read
`CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = ms1[i, j + c]  if 0 <= j + c < sqrt(AME_NELEM), otherwise
md[i,j] = zero(Md[md]).
+
Elements shifted beyond the row boundary are filled with zero (no wrap-around).
For the row-shift form, see `mrowshift.ew.x`.
+
The common datatype size is no smaller than `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`; packed
datatypes are not supported.

instructions.name: mcolunzip.ew
instructions.synopsis: Column unzip (de-interleave columns from two inputs)
instructions.description:
De-interleaves the columns of the two-square logical source formed by the
logical source square at `ms1` followed by the logical source square at `ms2`
into the two destination operands `D0` and `D1`.
+
Let `N = sqrt(AME_NELEM)`. For each row `i` and index `j` in `[0, N/2)`:
+
D0[i, j]         = A[i, 2j]
D0[i, N/2 + j]   = B[i, 2j]
D1[i, j]         = A[i, 2j+1]
D1[i, N/2 + j]   = B[i, 2j+1]
+
where `A` and `B` are the logical source squares at `ms1` and `ms2`.
Even-indexed columns of the logical source are collected into `D0`;
odd-indexed columns into `D1`.  Each source is its sole square.
+
The common datatype size is no smaller than `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`; packed
datatypes are not supported.
+
`D0` is the logical square at `md`, and `D1` occupies the consecutive M
registers immediately following `D0`.  A datatype wider than
`AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE` therefore spans multiple consecutive M registers per
destination operand.
+
`md` must be aligned to the combined register span of `D0` and `D1`
(even-aligned when each destination operand occupies a single M register).
Inverse of `mcolzip.ew`.

instructions.name: mcolzip.ew
instructions.synopsis: Column zip (interleave columns from two inputs)
instructions.description:
Interleaves columns from the logical source square at `ms1` and the logical
source square at `ms2` into the two destination operands `D0` and `D1`.
+
Let `N = sqrt(AME_NELEM)`. For each row `i` and index `j` in `[0, N/2)`:
+
D0[i, 2j]     = A[i, j]
D0[i, 2j+1]   = B[i, j]
D1[i, 2j]     = A[i, N/2 + j]
D1[i, 2j+1]   = B[i, N/2 + j]
+
where `A` and `B` are the logical source squares at `ms1` and `ms2`.
Columns from `A` appear at even positions and columns from `B` appear at
odd positions within the two-square logical destination.  Each source is its
sole square.
+
The common datatype size is no smaller than `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`; packed
datatypes are not supported.
+
`D0` is the logical square at `md`, and `D1` occupies the consecutive M
registers immediately following `D0`.  A datatype wider than
`AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE` therefore spans multiple consecutive M registers per
destination operand.
+
`md` must be aligned to the combined register span of `D0` and `D1`
(even-aligned when each destination operand occupies a single M register).
Inverse of `mcolunzip.ew`.

instructions.name: mconv.ew
instructions.synopsis: Convert element data between supported datatypes, including packed and non-packed representations
instructions.description:
Converts element data between supported datatypes.
+
The source datatype is determined from `Md[ms1]` and the destination datatype from `Md[md]`.
The source and destination datatypes may each be a packed or a non-packed datatype; no
particular packedness combination is required.  Both operands are formed by the common
operand-formation rules, so the instruction's square count is `N_sq = max(pack_factor)`
and every operand spans exactly `N_sq` squares.
+
`mconv.ew` converts each element of the formed logical source operand from the source
datatype to the destination datatype and writes the result squares to the formed logical
destination operand.  A packed source with a non-packed destination therefore expands
the source squares; a non-packed source with a packed destination compresses them; and
operands with the same packedness convert each element without changing the square layout.
+
Element conversion follows the common datatype conversion rules; unsupported conversion tuples set
`amestatus.UN` and do not modify any register.
instructions.operation: D = convert(A) over every element of the formed logical operands

instructions.name: mbcast.m.x
instructions.synopsis: Convert an X-register scalar and broadcast it to an M operand
instructions.description:
Interprets the low 32 bits of `X[xtyp]` as an AME datatype encoding and the
X-register bit pattern as one scalar of that datatype, where
`src_dtype = X[xtyp][31:0]`.  If `sizeof(src_dtype)` is less than XLEN, only
the low `sizeof(src_dtype)` bits are used and higher X-register bits are
ignored; if it is greater than XLEN, `X[xs1]` is zero-extended to that width.
The
scalar is converted once to the destination datatype `Md[md]` using the
common scalar conversion rules, then the converted value is written to every
logical element of `M[md]`.  Packed destinations receive the value in every
logical packed element.
+
The source and destination datatype encodings must be supported, and the
source-to-destination conversion must be supported.  Otherwise,
`amestatus.UN` is set and no destination state is modified.  The instruction
does not read `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`; the source datatype is its explicit
`xtyp` operand.
instructions.operation: D[i] = convert(X[xs1], source datatype X[xtyp], destination datatype Md[md])

instructions.name: mcos.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise cosine of `ms1`, stored into `md`.
+
This instruction is defined only for floating-point datatypes. If the datatype of
`md` or `ms1` is not a supported floating-point type, `amestatus.UN` is set and no
register is written.
+
The numerical precision of the result is implementation-defined.

instructions.name: mexp2.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise base-2 exponentiation of the tensor in `ms1`, stored into `md`.
+
For each element, `md[i] = 2^ms1[i]`.

instructions.name: mfrintm.ew
instructions.description:
Rounds each floating-point element of `ms1` to an integral value toward minus infinity (floor), stored into `md`.
+
This instruction is defined only for floating-point datatypes. If the datatype of
`md` or `ms1` is not a supported floating-point type, `amestatus.UN` is set and no
register is written.

instructions.name: mfrintn.ew
instructions.synopsis: Round float to integral (nearest, ties to even)
instructions.description:
Rounds each floating-point element of `ms1` to the nearest integral value, with ties rounded to even, stored into `md`.
+
This instruction is defined only for floating-point datatypes. If the datatype of
`md` or `ms1` is not a supported floating-point type, `amestatus.UN` is set and no
register is written.

instructions.name: mfrintp.ew
instructions.description:
Rounds each floating-point element of `ms1` to an integral value toward positive infinity (ceil), stored into `md`.
+
This instruction is defined only for floating-point datatypes. If the datatype of
`md` or `ms1` is not a supported floating-point type, `amestatus.UN` is set and no
register is written.

instructions.name: mfrintz.ew
instructions.description:
Rounds each floating-point element of `ms1` to an integral value toward zero (truncate), stored into `md`.
+
This instruction is defined only for floating-point datatypes. If the datatype of
`md` or `ms1` is not a supported floating-point type, `amestatus.UN` is set and no
register is written.

instructions.name: mgettyp
instructions.description:
Gets the 32-bit datatype descriptor of an `M` register by reading from `Md`
and zero-extending it to XLEN in `X[xd]`.

instructions.name: mhdiff.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise half-difference of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.
Computes the true half-difference; pairs with `mmean.ew`.

instructions.name: mhdiff.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise half-difference between a scalar constant from integer register
`xs1` and every element of square `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
The type of the scalar is determined by `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`. The scalar is converted
to the datatype of `ms2` before the operation and then applied to every element position `i`:
+
md[i] = (xs1 - ms2[i]) / 2
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mldexp.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise scale of `ms1` by a power of two given by `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
For each element, `md[i] = ms1[i] * 2^ms2[i]`.
+
Equivalent to C `ldexp` applied elementwise.
Complementary to `mrdexp.ew`.

instructions.name: mldexp.ew.x
instructions.description:
Scales every element of square `ms2` by a power of two given by a scalar integer
from integer register `xs1`, stored into `md`.
+
For each element position `i`:
+
md[i] = ms2[i] * 2^xs1
+
The type of the matrix elements is determined by `Md[ms2]`. `X[xs1]` is
zero-extended or low-bit truncated to the width of
<<ame:doc:param:AME_MAX_INT_DTYPE,AME_MAX_INT_DTYPE>> and then interpreted using
that integer datatype.  The exponent is a fixed-type control operand and does
not read `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`.
+
Equivalent to C `ldexp` applied elementwise with a broadcast scalar exponent.
Complementary to `mrdexp.ew`.
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mldexpacc.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise left-shift scale of `ms1` by a power of two given by `ms2`, accumulated into `md`.
+
For each element, `md[i] = md[i] + ms1[i] * 2^ms2[i]`.
+
`md` is both a source and destination: the existing element is read, the scaled value
is added, and the sum is written back.
+
Complementary to `mrdexpacc.ew`.

instructions.name: mldexpacc.ew.x
instructions.description:
Scales every element of square `ms2` by a power of two given by a scalar integer
from integer register `xs1`, accumulated into `md`.
+
For each element position `i`:
+
md[i] = md[i] + ms2[i] * 2^xs1
+
`md` is both a source and destination: the existing element is read, the scaled value
is added, and the sum is written back.
+
The type of the matrix elements is determined by `Md[ms2]`. `X[xs1]` is
zero-extended or low-bit truncated to the width of
<<ame:doc:param:AME_MAX_INT_DTYPE,AME_MAX_INT_DTYPE>> and then interpreted using
that integer datatype.  The exponent is a fixed-type control operand and does
not read `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`.
+
Complementary to `mrdexpacc.ew`.
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mlog2.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise base-2 logarithm of the tensor in `ms1`, stored into `md`.
+
For each element, `md[i] = log2(ms1[i])`.

instructions.name: mlog2sub.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise biased base-2 logarithm: subtracts `ms2` from the base-2 logarithm
of the absolute value of `ms1`, stored into `md`.
+
For each element, `md[i] = log2(|ms1[i]|) - ms2[i]`.
+
Useful for biased-exponent arithmetic, where `ms2` holds the bias value.
Complementary to `msublog2.ew`.

instructions.name: mlog2sub.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise base-2 logarithm of the absolute value of every element of
square `ms2`, minus a scalar bias from integer register `xs1`, stored into `md`.
+
The type of the scalar is determined by `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`. The scalar is converted
to the datatype of `ms2` before being used as the bias for every element position `i`:
+
md[i] = log2(|ms2[i]|) - xs1
+
Useful for biased-exponent arithmetic, where `xs1` holds the bias value.
Complementary to `msublog2.ew.x`.
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mls
instructions.synopsis: Load raw M register from implementation-defined format
instructions.description:
Loads exactly one physical M register from memory in the implementation-defined
register format into matrix register `md`.
+
The data in memory must have been previously stored in the implementation-defined
register format (e.g., by a matching `mss` instruction). No datatype conversion is
performed; the in-memory layout is the exact physical-register representation.
The datatype in `Md[md]` is not interpreted.  Consequently, packed sub-squares
resident in `md` are transferred together, while a wide logical square requires
one `mls` for each physical M register in its group.
+
For portable interoperability with other implementations, use
<<ame:doc:inst:mls_rm,mls.rm>> or <<ame:doc:inst:mls_cm,mls.cm>>.
+
The transfer size is `AME_MATRIX_REGISTER_SIZE / 8` bytes.  The address must
be aligned to that size or 4KB, whichever is smaller. Otherwise, `mls` raises
a `Load Misaligned` exception.

instructions.name: mls.cm
instructions.description:
Loads a square from memory in column-major format into matrix register `md`.
+
The datatype is determined from `Md[md]`. For compute datatypes
(size >= `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`), one square is loaded. For packed datatypes
(size < `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`), `pack_factor = AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE / sizeof(Md[md])`
squares are loaded and packed into a single M register.
+
The data in memory is stored contiguously in column-major order: within each sub-square,
column `j` immediately follows column `j-1` with no padding. All elements are loaded
unconditionally.
+
Let `total_bytes = ceil(pack_factor * AME_NELEM * sizeof(Md[md]) / 8)`.
The address must be aligned to `total_bytes` or 4KB, whichever is smaller.
Otherwise, `mls.cm` raises a `Load Misaligned` exception.

instructions.name: mls.rm
instructions.description:
Loads a square from memory in row-major format into matrix register `md`.
+
The datatype is determined from `Md[md]`. For compute datatypes
(size >= `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`), one square is loaded. For packed datatypes
(size < `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`), `pack_factor = AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE / sizeof(Md[md])`
squares are loaded and packed into a single M register.
+
The data in memory is stored contiguously in row-major order: within each sub-square,
row `i` immediately follows row `i-1` with no padding. All elements are loaded
unconditionally.
+
Let `total_bytes = ceil(pack_factor * AME_NELEM * sizeof(Md[md]) / 8)`.
The address must be aligned to `total_bytes` or 4KB, whichever is smaller.
Otherwise, `mls.rm` raises a `Load Misaligned` exception.

instructions.name: mls.st
instructions.synopsis: Load square from strided memory format
instructions.description:
Loads a square from memory in strided format into matrix register `md`.
+
The datatype is determined from `Md[md]`. For compute datatypes
(size >= `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`), one square is loaded. For packed datatypes
(size < `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`), `pack_factor = AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE / sizeof(Md[md])`
squares are loaded and packed into a single M register.
+
The strided load accesses memory as a sequence of equally spaced segments.
For non-packed datatypes, there are `sqrt(AME_NELEM)` segments, one per row, each
containing `sqrt(AME_NELEM)` contiguous elements.
For packed datatypes, there are still `sqrt(AME_NELEM)` segments, but each segment
contains `pack_factor * sqrt(AME_NELEM)` contiguous elements — `pack_factor` sub-squares
placed side by side horizontally within each row.

instructions.name: mmov.m.a
instructions.synopsis: Elementwise unconditional move from accumulator to M register
instructions.description:
Copies the source square from the accumulator operand to the M register `md`.
+

must match; if they differ, `amestatus.UN` is set and `md` is left unchanged.
+

datatype occupies a group of consecutive M registers.

`pack_factor` consecutive accumulators starting at `acc` each hold one
`N x N` square, and all `pack_factor` squares are packed into the single M
register `md`.  If `pack_factor` exceeds
<<ame:doc:param:AME_NUM_ACC_REGS,AME_NUM_ACC_REGS>>, `amestatus.UN` is set and
`md` is left unchanged.  Otherwise, every derived accumulator index in
`acc .. acc + pack_factor - 1` is checked according to
<<ame:doc:param:AME_UNIMPL_ACC_BEHAVIOR,AME_UNIMPL_ACC_BEHAVIOR>> before any
accumulator data is read or `md` is written; a failing check cannot cause a
partial transfer.

`md` must be a multiple of the number of M registers consumed by one element.
+

`Md[md]`.  As with any register group, the `Md` and `Ad` values of the
remaining registers in either group are ignored, and this instruction does
not modify any `Md` or `Ad` register.

derived index in that complete accumulator span is checked according to

source data is read or accumulator is written; a failing check cannot cause a
partial transfer.

remaining registers in either group are ignored, and this instruction does
not modify any `Md` or `Ad` register.

instructions.name: mmove8.m.x
instructions.synopsis: Move one 8-bit scalar into an M register position (debug)
instructions.description:
Writes the low 8 bits of `X[xs2]` into one 8-bit element position of the
single M register `md`.  The contents of `md` are viewed, in row-major order, as
`N = sqrt(AME_NELEM)` rows of `row_elements = (N * AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE) / 8`
8-bit elements each, independent of the configured datatype `Md[md]`.
+
The element position `pos` is selected by the low `log2(N * row_elements)`
bits of `X[xs1]`; higher bits are ignored.  The selected column is
`pos % row_elements` and the selected row is `pos / row_elements`.
+
This instruction is intended for debugging.  The element size is defined by
the instruction itself: it does not read `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`, does not
read or convert using `Md[md]`, does not form a register group, and never
sets `amestatus.UN`.  The register contents are first normalized with the
row-major layout transformation, using the unsigned integer datatype of
size `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`, for which exactly one square occupies one M
register; the normalized image is then reinterpreted, by bit slicing, as
`N` rows of `row_elements` elements of the instruction's element size.
Both steps are defined independently of the implementation register
layout, so the position-to-element mapping is identical on every
implementation.  If one row of the row-major
view is narrower than the element size, an `Illegal Instruction` exception
is raised.

instructions.name: mmul.2d
instructions.description:
Computes the matrix product of `ms1` and `ms2` and stores the result into `acc`,
discarding any previous value in `acc`.
+
`acc[i,k] = sum over j of (ms1[i,j] * ms2[j,k])`
+
For the accumulating form, see `mmulacc.2d`.

instructions.name: mmul.ew
instructions.description: Elementwise multiplication of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.

instructions.name: mmul.ew.x
instructions.description:
Multiplies every element of square `ms2` by a scalar constant from integer register
`xs1`, stored into `md`.
+
The type of the scalar is determined by `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`. The scalar is converted
to the datatype of `ms2` before the operation and then applied to every element position `i`:
+
md[i] = xs1 × ms2[i]
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mmulacc.2d
instructions.description:
Accumulates the matrix product of `ms1` and `ms2` into `acc`.
+
`acc[i,k] += sum over j of (ms1[i,j] * ms2[j,k])`
+
`acc` is both a source and destination: its current value is read, the matrix
product is added, and the result is written back.
+
For the non-accumulating form, see `mmul.2d`.
For the subtracting form, see `mmulaccneg.2d`.

instructions.name: mmulacc.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise multiply-accumulate: multiplies `ms1` by `ms2` elementwise and accumulates
into `md`.
+
`md` is both a source and destination: the existing element is read, the product
`ms1[i] × ms2[i]` is added, and the sum is written back.
+
For each element position `i`:
+
md[i] = md[i] + ms1[i] × ms2[i]

instructions.name: mmulacc.ew.x
instructions.description:

+
`md` is both a source and destination: the existing element is read, the scaled value
`xs1 × ms2[i]` is added, and the sum is written back.
+
The type of the scalar is determined by `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`. The scalar is converted
to the datatype of `ms2` before the operation and then applied to every element position `i`:
+
md[i] = md[i] + xs1 × ms2[i]
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mmulaccneg.2d
instructions.description:

+
`acc[i,k] -= sum over j of (ms1[i,j] * ms2[j,k])`
+
`acc` is both a source and destination: its current value is read, the matrix
product is subtracted, and the result is written back.
+
For the adding accumulate form, see `mmulacc.2d`.

+
For each element position `i`:
+

`acc[i,k] += sum over j of (ms1[j,i] * ms2[j,k])`
+
`acc` is both a source and destination: its current value is read, the transposed-A
matrix product is added, and the result is written back.
+
For the non-accumulating form, see `mmulat.2d`.
instructions.operation: C = C + sum(transpose(A[s]) × B[s], s = 0 .. pack_factor-1)

instructions.name: mmulbt.2d
instructions.description:
Computes the matrix product of `ms1` with the transpose of `ms2` and stores the
result into `acc`, discarding any previous value in `acc`.
+
`acc[i,k] = sum over j of (ms1[i,j] * ms2[k,j])`
+
For the accumulating form, see `mmulbtacc.2d`.

instructions.name: mmulbtacc.2d
instructions.synopsis: Matrix multiply with transposed B, accumulate
instructions.description:
Accumulates the matrix product of `ms1` with the transpose of `ms2` into `acc`.
+
`acc[i,k] += sum over j of (ms1[i,j] * ms2[k,j])`
+
`acc` is both a source and destination: its current value is read, the transposed-B
matrix product is added, and the result is written back.
+
For the non-accumulating form, see `mmulbt.2d`.
instructions.operation: C = C + sum(A[s] × transpose(B[s]), s = 0 .. pack_factor-1)

instructions.name: mmulneg.2d
instructions.description:
Computes the negated matrix product of `ms1` and `ms2` and stores the result into `acc`,
discarding any previous value in `acc`.
+
`acc[i,k] = -(sum over j of (ms1[i,j] * ms2[j,k]))`
+
For the accumulating negated form, see `mmulaccneg.2d`.

instructions.name: mmulneg.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise negate-multiply of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
For each element position `i`:
+
md[i] = -(ms1[i] × ms2[i])

instructions.name: mmulneg.ew.x
instructions.description:
Negates the product of a scalar constant from integer register `xs1` and every element
of square `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
The type of the scalar is determined by `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`. The scalar is converted
to the datatype of `ms2` before the operation and then applied to every element position `i`:
+
md[i] = -(xs1 × ms2[i])
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mmulsub.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise fused multiply-subtract where `md` serves as both the multiplicand and the
destination.
+
`md` is both a source and destination: each existing element is multiplied by the
corresponding element of `ms2`, `ms1` is subtracted from that product, and the result
is written back. Note: this computes `ms1 - ms2 × md`, not `ms2 × md - ms1`.
+
For each element position `i`:
+
md[i] = ms1[i] - ms2[i] × md[i]

instructions.name: mmulsub.ew.x
instructions.description:
Elementwise scalar fused multiply-subtract where `md` serves as both the multiplicand
and the destination.
+
`md` is both a source and destination: each existing element is multiplied by the
corresponding element of `ms2`, that product is subtracted from the scalar `xs1`,
and the result is written back.
+
The type of the scalar is determined by `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`. The scalar is converted
to the datatype of `ms2` before the operation and then applied to every element position `i`:
+
md[i] = xs1 - ms2[i] × md[i]
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mor.ew
instructions.description: Elementwise bitwise OR of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.

instructions.name: mor.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise bitwise OR of a scalar constant from integer register `xs1`
with every element of square `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
The type of the scalar is determined by `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`. The scalar is converted
to the datatype of `ms2` before the operation and then applied to every element position `i`:
+
md[i] = xs1 | ms2[i]
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mornot.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise bitwise OR of `ms1` with the bitwise complement of `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
Useful for setting bits: any bit clear in `ms2` will be set in the result.

instructions.name: mornot.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise bitwise OR of a scalar constant from integer register `xs1`
with the bitwise complement of every element of square `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
The type of the scalar is determined by `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`. The scalar is converted
to the datatype of `ms2` before the operation and then applied to every element position `i`:
+
md[i] = xs1 | ~ms2[i]
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mpack.ew.x
instructions.synopsis: Pack one square into a slot of a packed M register
instructions.description:
Inserts the single non-packed square group beginning at `ms1` into the sub-square slot selected by the
index in integer register `xs1` of the packed M register `md`, converting each element
from the non-packed datatype (`Md[ms1]`) to the packed datatype (`Md[md]`). The other
sub-square slots of `md` are preserved (read-modify-write).
+
`Md[md]` must be a packed datatype and `Md[ms1]` a non-packed datatype; otherwise
`amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written. The index must be less than
`pack_factor = AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE / sizeof(Md[md])`; an out-of-range index raises an
`Illegal Instruction` exception.
The index is a fixed U32 unsigned integer control operand (the low 32 bits of
`X[xs1]`) and does not read
`CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`.
+
This is the single-square form of the pack (compress) direction of
<<ame:doc:inst:mconv_ew,mconv.ew>>; use it to pack one square at a time without holding
all `pack_factor` non-packed squares in registers simultaneously.

instructions.name: mprefixadd.col
instructions.description:
Computes an inclusive prefix sum (running sum) along each column of `ms1`, stored into `md`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = sum over k <= i of ms1[k,j]
+
`md[0,j] = ms1[0,j]`, `md[1,j] = ms1[0,j] + ms1[1,j]`, and so on.
For the row prefix-sum form, see `mprefixadd.row`.
For the column max-scan form, see `mprefixmax.col`.

instructions.name: mprefixadd.row
instructions.description:
Computes an inclusive prefix sum (running sum) along each row of `ms1`, stored into `md`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = sum over k <= j of ms1[i,k]
+
`md[i,0] = ms1[i,0]`, `md[i,1] = ms1[i,0] + ms1[i,1]`, and so on.
For the row max-scan form, see `mprefixmax.row`.
For the column add-scan form, see `mprefixadd.col`.

instructions.name: mprefixmax.col
instructions.description:
Computes a running maximum (inclusive prefix max) along each column of `ms1`, stored into `md`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = max over k <= i of ms1[k,j]
+
`md[0,j] = ms1[0,j]`, `md[1,j] = max(ms1[0,j], ms1[1,j])`, and so on.
For the row prefix-max form, see `mprefixmax.row`.
For the column add-scan form, see `mprefixadd.col`.

instructions.name: mprefixmax.row
instructions.description:
Computes a running maximum (inclusive prefix max) along each row of `ms1`, stored into `md`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = max over k <= j of ms1[i,k]
+
`md[i,0] = ms1[i,0]`, `md[i,1] = max(ms1[i,0], ms1[i,1])`, and so on.
For the row add-scan form, see `mprefixadd.row`.
For the column max-scan form, see `mprefixmax.col`.

instructions.name: mrdexp.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise scale of `ms1` by a negative power of two given by `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
For each element, `md[i] = ms1[i] * 2^(-ms2[i])`.
+
Equivalent to `np.ldexp(ms1, -ms2)`.
Complementary to `mldexp.ew`.

instructions.name: mrdexpacc.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise right-shift scale of `ms1` by a negative power of two given by `ms2`,
accumulated into `md`.
+
For each element, `md[i] = md[i] + ms1[i] * 2^(-ms2[i])`.
+
`md` is both a source and destination: the existing element is read, the scaled value
is added, and the sum is written back.
+
Complementary to `mldexpacc.ew`.

instructions.name: mrec.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise reciprocal of `ms1`, stored into `md`.
+
This instruction is defined only for floating-point datatypes. If the datatype of
`md` or `ms1` is not a supported floating-point type, `amestatus.UN` is set and no
register is written.
+
The numerical precision of the result is implementation-defined.

instructions.name: mreduceadd.col
instructions.description:
Reduces each column of `ms1` by addition and broadcasts the result to all rows of the
corresponding column in `md`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = sum over k of ms1[k,j]
+
All rows in each output column receive the same value (the column sum).
For the row-reduction form, see `mreduceadd.row`.
For the column max-reduction form, see `mreducemax.col`.

instructions.name: mreduceadd.row
instructions.description:
Reduces each row of `ms1` by addition and broadcasts the result to all columns of the
corresponding row in `md`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = sum over k of ms1[i,k]
+
All columns in each output row receive the same value (the row sum).
For the row max-reduction form, see `mreducemax.row`.
For the column add-reduction form, see `mreduceadd.col`.

instructions.name: mreducemax.col
instructions.description:
Reduces each column of `ms1` by maximum and broadcasts the result to all rows of the
corresponding column in `md`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = max over k of ms1[k,j]
+
All rows in each output column receive the same value (the column maximum).
For the row-reduction form, see `mreducemax.row`.
For the column add-reduction form, see `mreduceadd.col`.

instructions.name: mreducemax.row
instructions.description:
Reduces each row of `ms1` by maximum and broadcasts the result to all columns of the
corresponding row in `md`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = max over k of ms1[i,k]
+
All columns in each output row receive the same value (the row maximum).
For the row add-reduction form, see `mreduceadd.row`.
For the column max-reduction form, see `mreducemax.col`.

instructions.name: mreducemin.col
instructions.description:
Reduces each column of `ms1` by minimum and broadcasts the result to all rows of the
corresponding column in `md`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = min over k of ms1[k,j]
+
All rows in each output column receive the same value (the column minimum).
For the row-reduction form, see `mreducemin.row`.
For the column max-reduction form, see `mreducemax.col`.

instructions.name: mreducemin.row
instructions.description:
Reduces each row of `ms1` by minimum and broadcasts the result to all columns of the
corresponding row in `md`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = min over k of ms1[i,k]
+
All columns in each output row receive the same value (the row minimum).
For the column-reduction form, see `mreducemin.col`.
For the row max-reduction form, see `mreducemax.row`.

instructions.name: mrowbcast.ew.x
instructions.synopsis: Broadcast one row to all rows
instructions.description:
Broadcasts row `c` (from integer register `xs1`) of `ms1` to every row of `md`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = ms1[c, j]
+
If `c` is outside `[0, sqrt(AME_NELEM))`, an `Illegal Instruction` exception is raised.
+
The `xs1` operand is a control scalar: its low 32 bits are interpreted as an
unsigned integer row index.  It does not read `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]` and does not undergo
AME datatype conversion.
+
The common datatype size is no smaller than `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`; packed
datatypes are not supported.

instructions.name: mrowgather.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise row gather: for each element in each column, uses the corresponding index from `ms2`
to select a row from the same column of `ms1`, and stores the result into `md`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = ms1[ms2[i,j], j]
+
`ms2` provides integer row indices in the range `[0, sqrt(AME_NELEM))`.
An out-of-range index raises an `Illegal Instruction` exception.
+
The common datatype size is no smaller than `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`; packed
datatypes are not supported.

instructions.name: mrowid.ew
instructions.synopsis: Write zero-based row index to every element
instructions.description:
Writes to each element of the M register group `md` the zero-based index of
the row containing that element.  With `N = sqrt(AME_NELEM)`, every
element of row `i` receives the value `i`, for `0 <= i < N`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = i
+
The index value is represented in the destination datatype `Md[md]`.  The
destination datatype must be a supported *integer* datatype in which the
largest index `N-1` is exactly representable; otherwise `amestatus.UN` is
set and no register is written.
+
Together with `<<ame:doc:inst:mcolid_ew,mcolid.ew>>`, this instruction forms
the index group of the 1-dimensional elementwise instructions, typically
used to materialize coordinate operands for gather, scatter, and predication
sequences.

instructions.name: mrowshift.ew.x
instructions.synopsis: Elementwise row shift by scalar offset
instructions.description:
Elementwise row shift of `ms1` by offset `c`, obtained by interpreting the
low 32 bits of integer register `xs1` as a signed two's-complement integer,
stored into `md`.  This fixed-type control operand does not read
`CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i,j] = ms1[i+c, j]  if 0 <= i+c < sqrt(AME_NELEM), otherwise
md[i,j] = zero(Md[md]).
+
Elements shifted beyond the column boundary are filled with zero (no wrap-around).
For the column-shift form, see `mcolshift.ew.x`.
+
The common datatype size is no smaller than `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`; packed
datatypes are not supported.

instructions.name: mrowunzip.ew
instructions.synopsis: Row unzip (de-interleave rows from two inputs)
instructions.description:
De-interleaves the rows of the two-square logical source formed by the logical
source square at `ms1` followed by the logical source square at `ms2` into the
two destination operands `D0` and `D1`.
+
Let `N = sqrt(AME_NELEM)`. For each row `k` in `[0, N/2)` and column `j`:
+
D0[k, j]       = A[2k, j]
D0[k+N/2, j]   = B[2k, j]
D1[k, j]       = A[2k+1, j]
D1[k+N/2, j]   = B[2k+1, j]
+
where `A` and `B` are the logical source squares at `ms1` and `ms2`.
Even-indexed rows of the logical source are collected into `D0`; odd-indexed
rows into `D1`.  Each source is its sole square.
+
The common datatype size is no smaller than `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`; packed
datatypes are not supported.
+
`D0` is the logical square at `md`, and `D1` occupies the consecutive M
registers immediately following `D0`.  A datatype wider than
`AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE` therefore spans multiple consecutive M registers per
destination operand.
+
`md` must be aligned to the combined register span of `D0` and `D1`
(even-aligned when each destination operand occupies a single M register).
Inverse of `mrowzip.ew`.

instructions.name: mrowzip.ew
instructions.synopsis: Row zip (interleave rows from two inputs)
instructions.description:
Interleaves rows from the logical source square at `ms1` and the logical
source square at `ms2` into the two destination operands `D0` and `D1`.
+
Let `N = sqrt(AME_NELEM)`. For each row `k` in `[0, N/2)` and column `j`:
+
D0[2k, j]     = A[k, j]
D0[2k+1, j]   = B[k, j]
D1[2k, j]     = A[N/2+k, j]
D1[2k+1, j]   = B[N/2+k, j]
+
where `A` and `B` are the logical source squares at `ms1` and `ms2`.
Rows from `A` appear at even positions and rows from `B` appear at odd
positions within the two-square logical destination.  Each source is its
sole square.
+
The common datatype size is no smaller than `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`; packed
datatypes are not supported.
+
`D0` is the logical square at `md`, and `D1` occupies the consecutive M
registers immediately following `D0`.  A datatype wider than
`AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE` therefore spans multiple consecutive M registers per
destination operand.
+
`md` must be aligned to the combined register span of `D0` and `D1`
(even-aligned when each destination operand occupies a single M register).
Inverse of `mrowunzip.ew`.

instructions.name: mrsqrt.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise reciprocal square root of `ms1`, stored into `md`.
+
This instruction is defined only for floating-point datatypes. If the datatype of
`md` or `ms1` is not a supported floating-point type, `amestatus.UN` is set and no
register is written.
+
The numerical precision of the result is implementation-defined.

instructions.name: mrowscatadd.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise row scatter-add: routes each element of `ms1` to a destination row
in `md` determined by the corresponding index in `ms2`, and accumulates with addition.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[ms2[i,j], j] += ms1[i,j]
+
`md` is both a source and destination: elements at the target columns are read,
the contribution from `ms1` is added, and the result is written back.
+
`ms2` provides integer row indices in the range `[0, sqrt(AME_NELEM))`.
Multiple elements may scatter to the same destination row; all contributions are accumulated.
An out-of-range index raises an `Illegal Instruction` exception.
+
For the column scatter-add form, see `mcolscatadd.ew`.
For the row scatter-max form, see `mrowscatmax.ew`.
+
The common datatype size is no smaller than `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`; packed
datatypes are not supported.

instructions.name: mcolscatadd.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise column scatter-add: routes each element of `ms1` to a destination column
in `md` determined by the corresponding index in `ms2`, and accumulates with addition.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i, ms2[i,j]] += ms1[i,j]
+
`md` is both a source and destination: elements at the target rows are read,
the contribution from `ms1` is added, and the result is written back.
+
`ms2` provides integer column indices in the range `[0, sqrt(AME_NELEM))`.
Multiple elements may scatter to the same destination column; all contributions are accumulated.
An out-of-range index raises an `Illegal Instruction` exception.
+
For the column scatter-max form, see `mcolscatmax.ew`.
For the row scatter-add form, see `mrowscatadd.ew`.
+
The common datatype size is no smaller than `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`; packed
datatypes are not supported.

instructions.name: mrowscatmax.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise row scatter-max: routes each element of `ms1` to a destination row
in `md` determined by the corresponding index in `ms2`, and accumulates with maximum.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[ms2[i,j], j] = max(md[ms2[i,j], j], ms1[i,j])
+
`md` is both a source and destination: elements at the target columns are read,
the maximum with the incoming value is taken, and the result is written back.
+
`ms2` provides integer row indices in the range `[0, sqrt(AME_NELEM))`.
Multiple elements may scatter to the same destination row; all contributions are reduced.
An out-of-range index raises an `Illegal Instruction` exception.
+
For the column scatter-max form, see `mcolscatmax.ew`.
For the row scatter-add form, see `mrowscatadd.ew`.
+
The common datatype size is no smaller than `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`; packed
datatypes are not supported.

instructions.name: mcolscatmax.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise column scatter-max: routes each element of `ms1` to a destination column
in `md` determined by the corresponding index in `ms2`, and accumulates with maximum.
+
For each row `i` and column `j`:
+
md[i, ms2[i,j]] = max(md[i, ms2[i,j]], ms1[i,j])
+
`md` is both a source and destination: elements at the target rows are read,
the maximum with the incoming value is taken, and the result is written back.
+
`ms2` provides integer column indices in the range `[0, sqrt(AME_NELEM))`.
Multiple elements may scatter to the same destination column; all contributions are reduced.
An out-of-range index raises an `Illegal Instruction` exception.
+
For the column scatter-add form, see `mcolscatadd.ew`.
For the row scatter-max form, see `mrowscatmax.ew`.
+
The common datatype size is no smaller than `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`; packed
datatypes are not supported.

instructions.name: mselge.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise predicated select using the non-negative sign of `ms1` to gate `ms2` into `md`.
+
For each element, `md[i] = ms2[i]` if `ms1[i] >= 0` (sign bit clear),
otherwise `md[i] = 0`.
+
`ms1` serves as the predicate register: any non-negative value is treated as true.
This allows comparison results or arithmetic sign values to be used directly
as predicates without normalization.
+
Complementary to `msellt.ew`.

instructions.name: msellt.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise predicated select using the sign of `ms1` to gate `ms2` into `md`.
+
For each element, `md[i] = ms2[i]` if `ms1[i] < 0` (sign bit set),
otherwise `md[i] = 0`.
+
`ms1` serves as the predicate register: any negative value is treated as true.
This allows comparison results or arithmetic sign values to be used directly
as predicates without normalization.
+
Complementary to `mselge.ew`.

instructions.name: msettyp
instructions.description:
Sets `Md[md]` to the low 32 bits of `X[xs1]` and clears every physical storage bit
in the complete M-register group required by that new datatype.  This is a
raw-bit clear, not conversion to the new datatype's semantic zero.  The group
base must meet the new datatype's alignment requirement and its complete span
must fit in the implemented M register file.  Upper X-register bits are ignored.
instructions.operation:
new_dtype = X[xs1][31:0]
group_size = max(1, ceil(sizeof(new_dtype) / AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE))
Md[md] = new_dtype; raw_bits(M[md .. md+group_size-1]) = 0

instructions.name: msin.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise sine of `ms1`, stored into `md`.
+
This instruction is defined only for floating-point datatypes. If the datatype of
`md` or `ms1` is not a supported floating-point type, `amestatus.UN` is set and no
register is written.
+
The numerical precision of the result is implementation-defined.

instructions.name: msll.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise logical left shift of `ms1` by the per-element shift amount in `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
Only the low `lg2(EW)` bits of each shift-amount value are used, where `EW` is the
element width in bits of `ms1`. Shift amounts are interpreted as unsigned bit patterns.

instructions.name: msll.ew.x
instructions.description:
Logical left shift of every element of `ms2` by a scalar amount from integer register `xs1`, stored into `md`.
+
Only the low `lg2(EW)` bits of the scalar shift amount are used, where `EW` is the
element width in bits of `ms2`. The shift amount is interpreted as an unsigned bit pattern.
The X operand is a fixed unsigned integer control value and does not read
`CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`.

instructions.name: msqrt.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise square root of `ms1`, stored into `md`.
+
This instruction is defined only for floating-point datatypes. If the datatype of
`md` or `ms1` is not a supported floating-point type, `amestatus.UN` is set and no
register is written.
+
The result is correctly rounded according to the destination datatype's rounding mode.

instructions.name: msra.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise arithmetic (sign-preserving) right shift of `ms1` by the per-element shift amount in `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
Only the low `lg2(EW)` bits of each shift-amount value are used, where `EW` is the
element width in bits of `ms1`. Shift amounts are interpreted as unsigned bit patterns.

instructions.name: msra.ew.x
instructions.description:
Arithmetic (sign-preserving) right shift of every element of `ms2` by a scalar amount from integer register `xs1`, stored into `md`.
+
Only the low `lg2(EW)` bits of the scalar shift amount are used, where `EW` is the
element width in bits of `ms2`. The shift amount is interpreted as an unsigned bit pattern.
The X operand is a fixed unsigned integer control value and does not read
`CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`.

instructions.name: msrl.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise logical (unsigned) right shift of `ms1` by the per-element shift amount in `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
Only the low `lg2(EW)` bits of each shift-amount value are used, where `EW` is the
element width in bits of `ms1`. Shift amounts are interpreted as unsigned bit patterns.

instructions.name: msrl.ew.x
instructions.description:
Logical (unsigned) right shift of every element of `ms2` by a scalar amount from integer register `xs1`, stored into `md`.
+
Only the low `lg2(EW)` bits of the scalar shift amount are used, where `EW` is the
element width in bits of `ms2`. The shift amount is interpreted as an unsigned bit pattern.
The X operand is a fixed unsigned integer control value and does not read
`CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`.

instructions.name: mss
instructions.synopsis: Store raw M register in implementation-defined format
instructions.description:
Stores exactly one physical M register `ms1` into memory in the
implementation-defined register format.
+
The data written to memory is in the same implementation-defined format used by the
matching load instruction (`mls`). No datatype conversion is performed, and
the datatype in `Md[ms1]` is not interpreted.  Packed sub-squares resident in
`ms1` are transferred together, while a wide logical square requires one
`mss` for each physical M register in its group.
+
For portable interoperability with other implementations, use
<<ame:doc:inst:mss_rm,mss.rm>> or <<ame:doc:inst:mss_cm,mss.cm>>.
+
The transfer size is `AME_MATRIX_REGISTER_SIZE / 8` bytes.  The address must
be aligned to that size or 4KB, whichever is smaller. Otherwise, `mss` raises
a `Store/AMO Misaligned` exception.

instructions.name: mss.cm
instructions.description:
Stores a square from matrix register `ms1` into memory in column-major format.
+
The datatype is determined from `Md[ms1]`. For compute datatypes
(size >= `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`), one square is stored. For packed datatypes
(size < `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`), `pack_factor = AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE / sizeof(Md[ms1])`
squares are unpacked from the single M register and stored.
+
The data is written contiguously in column-major order: within each sub-square,
column `j` immediately follows column `j-1` with no padding. All elements are stored
unconditionally.
+
Let `total_bytes = ceil(pack_factor * AME_NELEM * sizeof(Md[ms1]) / 8)`.
The address must be aligned to `total_bytes` or 4KB, whichever is smaller.
Otherwise, `mss.cm` raises a `Store/AMO Misaligned` exception.

instructions.name: mss.rm
instructions.description:
Stores a square from matrix register `ms1` into memory in row-major format.
+
The datatype is determined from `Md[ms1]`. For compute datatypes
(size >= `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`), one square is stored. For packed datatypes
(size < `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`), `pack_factor = AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE / sizeof(Md[ms1])`
squares are unpacked from the single M register and stored.
+
The data is written contiguously in row-major order: within each sub-square,
row `i` immediately follows row `i-1` with no padding. All elements are stored
unconditionally.
+
Let `total_bytes = ceil(pack_factor * AME_NELEM * sizeof(Md[ms1]) / 8)`.
The address must be aligned to `total_bytes` or 4KB, whichever is smaller.
Otherwise, `mss.rm` raises a `Store/AMO Misaligned` exception.

instructions.name: mss.st
instructions.synopsis: Store square to strided memory format
instructions.description:
Stores a square from matrix register `ms1` into memory in strided format.
+
The datatype is determined from `Md[ms1]`. For compute datatypes
(size >= `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`), one square is stored. For packed datatypes
(size < `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`), `pack_factor = AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE / sizeof(Md[ms1])`
squares are unpacked from the single M register and stored.
+
The strided store writes memory as a sequence of equally spaced segments.
For non-packed datatypes, there are `sqrt(AME_NELEM)` segments, one per row, each
containing `sqrt(AME_NELEM)` contiguous elements.
For packed datatypes, there are still `sqrt(AME_NELEM)` segments, but each segment
contains `pack_factor * sqrt(AME_NELEM)` contiguous elements — `pack_factor` sub-squares
placed side by side horizontally within each row.
Consecutive segments are separated by a byte stride supplied in integer register `xs2`.
+
Let `element_bytes = ceil(sizeof(Md[ms1]) / 8)`.  The address must be aligned
to `element_bytes` or 4KB, whichever is smaller. Otherwise, `mss.st` raises a
`Store/AMO Misaligned` exception.  Segment byte counts and sub-byte packing
follow the common memory rules.

instructions.name: mss.tst
instructions.synopsis: Store square to transposed strided memory format
instructions.description:
Stores a square from matrix register `ms1` into memory in transposed strided format.
+
The datatype is determined from `Md[ms1]`. For compute datatypes
(size >= `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`), one square is stored. For packed datatypes
(size < `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`), `pack_factor = AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE / sizeof(Md[ms1])`
squares are unpacked from the single M register and stored.
+
The transposed strided store writes memory as a sequence of equally spaced segments,
one segment per column of the square. Each segment contains `sqrt(AME_NELEM)` contiguous
elements, and consecutive segments are separated by a byte stride supplied in integer
register `xs2`. For packed datatypes, the total number of segments is
`pack_factor * sqrt(AME_NELEM)` — one column per sub-square, stacked vertically.
The segment addresses and within-segment bit offsets are defined by the common
memory rules; this arrangement transposes each square during the transfer.
+
Let `element_bytes = ceil(sizeof(Md[ms1]) / 8)`.  The address must be aligned
to `element_bytes` or 4KB, whichever is smaller. Otherwise, `mss.tst` raises a
`Store/AMO Misaligned` exception.

instructions.name: msub.ew
instructions.description: Vector subtraction of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.

instructions.name: msub.ew.x
instructions.description:
Subtracts every element of square `ms2` from a scalar constant from integer register `xs1`,
stored into `md`.
+
The type of the scalar is determined by `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`. The scalar is converted
to the datatype of `ms2` before the operation and then applied to every element position `i`:
+
md[i] = xs1 - ms2[i]
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: msublog2.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise complementary biased base-2 logarithm: subtracts the base-2 logarithm
of the absolute value of `ms1` from `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
For each element, `md[i] = ms2[i] - log2(|ms1[i]|)`.
+
Useful for biased-exponent arithmetic, where `ms2` holds the bias value.
Complementary to `mlog2sub.ew`.

instructions.name: msublog2.ew.x
instructions.description:
Subtracts the elementwise base-2 logarithm of the absolute value of every element of
square `ms2` from a scalar constant from integer register `xs1`, stored into `md`.
+
The type of the scalar is determined by `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`. The scalar is converted
to the datatype of `ms2` before being used as the bias for every element position `i`:
+
md[i] = xs1 - log2(|ms2[i]|)
+
Useful for biased-exponent arithmetic, where `xs1` holds the bias value.
Complementary to `mlog2sub.ew.x`.
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mtanh.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise hyperbolic tangent of `ms1`, stored into `md`.
+
This instruction is defined only for floating-point datatypes. If the datatype of
`md` or `ms1` is not a supported floating-point type, `amestatus.UN` is set and no
register is written.
+
The numerical precision of the result is implementation-defined.

instructions.name: munpack.ew.x
instructions.synopsis: Unpack one sub-square from a packed M register
instructions.description:
Extracts a single sub-square, selected by the index in integer register `xs1`, from the
packed M register `ms1` and writes it to the non-packed M register group beginning at `md`, converting each
element from the packed datatype (`Md[ms1]`) to the non-packed datatype (`Md[md]`).
+
`Md[ms1]` must be a packed datatype and `Md[md]` a non-packed datatype; otherwise
`amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written. The index must be less than
`pack_factor = AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE / sizeof(Md[ms1])`; an out-of-range index raises an
`Illegal Instruction` exception.
The index is a fixed U32 unsigned integer control operand (the low 32 bits of
`X[xs1]`) and does not read
`CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`.
+
This is the single-square form of the unpack (expand) direction of
<<ame:doc:inst:mconv_ew,mconv.ew>>; use it to unpack one square at a time and limit the
register pressure of fully expanding a packed register.

instructions.name: mxor.ew
instructions.description: Elementwise bitwise XOR of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.

instructions.name: mxor.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise bitwise XOR of a scalar constant from integer register `xs1`
with every element of square `ms2`, stored into `md`.
+
The type of the scalar is determined by `CSR[ame_scalar_dtype]`. The scalar is converted
to the datatype of `ms2` before the operation and then applied to every element position `i`:
+
md[i] = xs1 ^ ms2[i]
+
If either `Md[md]` or `Md[ms2]` is uninitialized (zero), or the datatype combination
is not supported, `amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mzero.2d.acc
instructions.description:
Writes zero to every element of `acc`.
+
Typically used to initialize an accumulator before a matrix multiply sequence.

instructions.name: mzero.2d.m
instructions.description:
Writes zero to every element of the M register group `md`.
+
Typically used to initialize a tensor register before an elementwise sequence.

instructions.name: fence.ame
instructions.synopsis: Order selected AME memory transfers before selected non-AME memory transfers
instructions.description:
Orders AME memory transfers selected by the predecessor bits (`pr`, `pw`) before
non-AME memory transfers selected by the successor bits (`sr`, `sw`):
+
--
* `pr` (bit 10) — predecessor set includes AME loads (reads from memory into `M` registers).
* `pw` (bit 9) — predecessor set includes AME stores (writes from `M` registers to memory).
* `sr` (bit 8) — successor set includes non-AME loads (reads into X, F, or V register files).
* `sw` (bit 7) — successor set includes non-AME stores (writes from X, F, or V register files).
--
+
When all four bits are set (`fence.ame sw, sr, pw, pr`), all AME memory transfers are
guaranteed to be globally visible before any subsequent non-AME memory transfer.
Clearing a bit excludes the corresponding transfer class from the ordering constraint.
At least one of `pr`/`pw` must be set, and at least one of `sr`/`sw` must be set;
otherwise the instruction executes as a NOP with no ordering effect.
+
This instruction is the AME-to-non-AME ordering primitive described in
<<ame-consistency-model>>. It does *not* order non-AME transfers before AME transfers;
for that direction, software must use the standard RISC-V `fence` instruction.
+
`fence.ame` has no source or destination register operands. The four fence bits
are encoded in the `rd` field position (bits 11:7), following the R1 instruction format.
instructions.operation: order AME predecessors selected by pr/pw before non-AME successors selected by sr/sw
